title: Demurrage and Detention Free Time: Chargeable Days, Slabs and Day Rates on the Final Invoice
content:
## Clauses in force

1. Work on the final invoice of a Demurrage and Detention Free Time record begins when none of the record's clocks is still running.
2. Only the days a clock uses after its free days are exhausted are chargeable.
3. Where a product keeps **separate** clocks, each clock prices its own chargeable days — demurrage rates on the demurrage clock, detention rates on the detention clock — and the slab scale starts again from its beginning on each of them.
4. On a product with a **combined** clock, the chargeable days are the days that come after the merged free time has run out. Such a day takes demurrage pricing for as long as the box remains within the terminal, and detention pricing once the box is out of it. For an import container the split falls at the full gate-out: that date and the days before it are demurrage, the days after it detention. For an export container it falls at the full gate-in: that date and the days before it are detention, the days after it demurrage.
5. Numbering the chargeable days in order, those numbered within the first slab length fall in slab 1, those beyond it but within the first two lengths combined in slab 2, those beyond that but within all three lengths combined in slab 3, and every later one in slab 4.
6. When the booking the container moves under has dangerous goods as its cargo type, the uplift percentage of the product raises the day rates of demurrage days, and of demurrage days alone.
7. The final invoice consists of at most one demurrage line and one detention line. Every line shows how many chargeable days it bills, the dates of the earliest and the latest of them, and the sum of their day rates taken to the cent; where a line would have no chargeable day, it is left out.

## Retired wording

Two sentences that formerly stood in this policy are **no longer in force**:

- that every day takes the rate belonging to its kind of clock, to its slab and to the class the equipment class map gives the container, superseded by the current rate-class basis for detention and demurrage days;
- that slab positions run continuously through every chargeable day of the record, superseded by the current slab-count basis for demurrage days.

## Reading the clauses

| Model | Where demurrage days come from | Where detention days come from |
|---|---|---|
| separate | the demurrage clock, beyond its free days | the detention clock, beyond its free days |
| combined, import | chargeable days on or before full gate-out | chargeable days after full gate-out |
| combined, export | chargeable days after full gate-in | chargeable days on or before full gate-in |

## Hypothetical illustration of clause 3

A separate-clock import record has 3 chargeable demurrage days and 7 chargeable detention days. On a scale whose first slab holds 5 days, all 3 demurrage days sit in slab 1; the detention clock starts its own scale, so its first 5 days are slab 1 and its last 2 are slab 2.

## Hypothetical illustration of clause 7

A record with chargeable demurrage days but a detention clock that never went beyond its free days receives a demurrage line only.

superseded_clauses: Each day is billed at the rate of its clock type, slab and the rate class of the container given by equipment_class_map
the slab position of a day is counted across the whole sequence of chargeable days
